_about: Optional store copy per kit, keyed by the kit's slug. Shown on the storefront card and product page. Every claim must be true of the files actually in the kit: no invented results, reviews, testimonials or guarantees. Fields: tagline (one sentence, <=170 chars), who_for (1-2 sentences), outcomes (3-6 short lines), file_notes (file name -> one line on what that file is and does).

freelance-proposal-kit.tagline: Turn "can you send me a quote?" into a proposal the client can say yes to, with three priced options and follow-ups for every stage.
freelance-proposal-kit.who_for: Solo freelancers and small studios who write proposals for client projects and want them to look professional without starting from a blank page each time.
outcomes: Send a clear, one-to-three-page proposal built on a completed example
Offer Essential, Standard and Complete options instead of a single yes/no price
Know exactly what to send at each stage after the proposal goes out
Catch the mistakes that lose work with a five-minute pre-send check
See which proposals win, at what price, and why

file_notes.README.md: Start here: what's in the kit, the order to use it in, and how to adapt it
file_notes.proposal-template.md: Fill-in proposal template plus a fully completed example to copy from
file_notes.pricing-options.md: How to build three priced options, with worked maths
file_notes.follow-up-emails.md: Seven short emails with timing, from sending the proposal to a polite close
file_notes.proposal-checklist.md: Pre-send checklist covering the client's problem, scope, price and terms
file_notes.proposal-tracker.csv: Spreadsheet to log every proposal, its options, follow-ups, outcome and why you won or lost
